newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INJURY-TIME GOAL ROBS CELTIC OF CHANCE TO GO TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY-TIME GOAL ROBS CELTIC OF CHANCE TO GO TOP.

text.p: An injury-time goal from captain Dave McPherson gave Hearts a 2-2 home draw on Sunday and prevented Celtic from going top of the Scottish premier division.
Celtic needed to win to go ahead of Rangers on goal difference and two goals from Dutch striker Pierre Van Hooydonk looked to have been enough for victory.
But McPherson headed in a cross from substitute Pasquale Bruno to keep his former club at the top of league with a quarter of the season gone.
Celtic made the breakthrough seven minutes from halftime when Simon Donnelly cleverly dummied a low cross and Van Hooydonk scored with a right-foot shot.
Celtic extended their lead after 51 minutes when Van Hooydonk rattled home a cross for his 50th goal for the club and his 10th of the season.
Hearts replied swiftly with Colin Cameron pouncing on a loose ball and scoring with a low shot which went in off the post.
Celtic hung on and looked to have done enough until McPherson's late strike brought Hearts a point.
